title: Sardegna Diesel Prices Push Past the National Average as August Winds Down
dek: Self-service Gasolio in Sardegna has climbed nearly 4 cents in a week, edging past the mainland average as the island keeps paying more at the pump.
body: As of August 24, self-service Benzina in Sardegna averaged €2.0243 per litre and self-service Gasolio €2.1636 — both a touch above the national self-service averages of €2.0228 and €2.1593. The gap is narrow, about half a cent on petrol and just over four cents on diesel, but it marks a shift: an island that often tracks close to the mainland average is now paying slightly more at the pump for both major fuels.

The trend behind those numbers is unmistakable. Over the past week, self-service Benzina in Sardegna rose from €1.9968 to €2.0243 (about +1.4 cents), while self-service Gasolio climbed even faster, from €2.1073 to €2.1636 (roughly +5.6 cents) — a steady, uninterrupted climb day after day. Meanwhile the island's station network stayed active: 679 stations registered and 613 reporting prices, a 90.3% reporting rate that sits right in line with the national figure of 90.5%, a sign the local network kept feeding fresh data through the whole run-up.

Tracking a single region this closely, day after day, against a live national baseline, isn't something you'd want to maintain by hand in a spreadsheet. Fuel Dashboard rebuilds itself every morning straight from Italy's MIMIT price feed, with no manual copy-pasting involved. It's a small but concrete example of what's possible when Claude Code handles the plumbing: a self-updating, always-current view of fuel prices across all twenty Italian regions, maintained by an automated pipeline instead of a person re-typing numbers into Excel.
pull_quote: Sardegna's self-service diesel has climbed nearly 6 cents in a week — and is now pricier than the Italian average.
caption:
🇮🇹 Today's regional spotlight: Sardegna, where self-service diesel just climbed past €2.16/litre — now pricier than the Italian mainland average, after a steady week-long rise of nearly 6 cents.

That's the kind of granular, day-by-day signal you get from Fuel Dashboard, a project that tracks self-service and full-service prices for Benzina, Gasolio, GPL and Metano across all 20 Italian regions — rebuilt automatically every single morning from Italy's official MIMIT price feed. No manual data entry, no stale spreadsheet. Check today's numbers, and every region, at https://adeo-blip.github.io/fuel-price-italy/.

Here's the part I think is genuinely interesting: this entire pipeline — data ingestion, regional rotation, article writing, and the live site — is built and maintained with Claude Code. What used to be a manually-updated Excel sheet is now a dashboard that fetches, processes, and republishes itself daily, with an AI agent even drafting the daily regional write-up. It's a small but concrete example of what AI-assisted development makes practical: infrastructure that would never have been worth building by hand.
